g.text: Use disagreement to choose the next test
Start with a concrete workflow and one consequential uncertainty.
Which accepted work product improves, and for whom?
Challenge whether faster generation saves total effort after review.
Name a measurable bottleneck rather than a favored tool.
Which consequential failure could ordinary review miss?
An unsupported fact, wrong period, unauthorized action or bypassed denial.
Correct refusal is a control success. Test the reviewer or judge as well.
What baseline, checks and cost evidence would change our view?
Record one candidate experiment and one unresolved question.
A missing prerequisite or “do not proceed” can be a useful outcome;
avoid forcing consensus or an immediate project commitment.
End of the 29-slide core briefing • Eight reference pages follow for independent study.
